rp-bec-01.back: Biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification: how BC sorts land by climate, plants and soil.

rp-bec-02.front: Name the Interior zones from the valley floor up.
rp-bec-02.back: BG Bunchgrass, PP Ponderosa pine, IDF Interior Douglas fir, MS Montane spruce, ESSF Engelmann spruce and subalpine fir, AT Alpine tundra. Big Pines In Many Elk Areas.

rp-bec-03.back: IDF = Interior Douglas fir zone. x = very dry, h = hot. 2 = the local variant.

rp-bec-04.front: First small letter of a subzone: what does it tell you?
rp-bec-04.back: How wet: x very dry, d dry, m moist, w wet, v very wet.

rp-bec-05.front: Second small letter of an Interior subzone?
rp-bec-05.back: How warm: h hot, w warm, m mild, k cool, c cold.

rp-bec-06.back: It sits in the rain shadow of the Coast Mountains. Pacific air drops its rain on the coast side.

rp-bec-07.front: Rain and snow a year near Mission versus Kamloops?
rp-bec-07.back: About 2,140 mm at Haney (Maple Ridge) versus about 242 mm at Kamloops: about 9 times more.

rp-bec-16.front: How far can mule deer migrate to winter in the PP and IDF?

rp-bec-17.back: Deer struggle past about 30 cm. Moose move freely to about 40 cm, with slight difficulty at 40 to 70 cm.

rp-bec-18.back: Ecosystems with frequent stand maintaining fires: BG, PP and IDF. Ground fires kept them open.
